name: AllTogether: Investigating the Efficacy of Spliced Prompt for Web Navigation using Large Language Models
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: AllTogether standardizes prompts for HTML-based web navigation and compares prompting with instruction fine-tuning. Its analysis examines how HTML context, interaction history, and current environmental feedback affect task execution.

name: Training a Vision Language Model as Smartphone Assistant
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Trains a smartphone assistant from sequences of screenshots paired with earlier actions. The model predicts UI-only interactions such as taps and swipes, with evaluation on Android in the Wild.

name: Identifying User Goals from UI Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Defines goal identification from observed UI trajectories and an evaluation method for comparing intent descriptions within the same interface context. Experiments reuse Android and web automation data to compare human and model inference of users’ detailed goals.

name: Dynamic Planning for LLM-based Graphical User Interface Automation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Dynamic Planning of Thoughts revises a mobile GUI plan using current environmental feedback and execution history. The study compares this planning strategy with long-dialogue prompting and examines its behavior on unfamiliar tasks and different language-model backbones.

name: ExACT: Teaching AI Agents to Explore with Reflective-MCTS and Exploratory Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v5). The reported agent evaluation is on VisualWebArena.
summary: ExACT combines reflective tree search with learning from search experience to help web agents explore, assess states and backtrack on VisualWebArena.

name: Large Language Models Empowered Personalized Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: PersonalWAB benchmarks personalized web tasks, while PUMA retrieves relevant past web behavior to adapt agents' instruction handling and actions.

name: Lightweight Neural App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: LiMAC combines a compact Action Transformer with a fine-tuned vision-language model for Android app control. It uses textual goals and histories of screenshots and UI trees to predict actions, with evaluation on two mobile-control datasets.

name: From Context to Action: Analysis of the Impact of State Representation and Context on the Generalization of Multi-Turn Web Navigation Agents
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.
summary: Analyzes how interaction history and webpage representation affect multiturn web-agent generalization across unfamiliar websites, task categories, and geographic settings.

name: Learn-by-interact: A Data-Centric Framework for Self-Adaptive Agents in Realistic Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its evaluations also include coding tasks alongside web and desktop environments.
summary: Learn-by-interact synthesizes agent interaction trajectories from documentation and derives instructions from their histories for training or in-context use across web and desktop tasks.

name: R2D2: Remembering, Replaying and Dynamic Decision Making with a Reflective Agentic Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The abstract evaluates R2D2 on WebArena.
summary: R2D2 gives web agents a replay-buffer map of visited pages and a reflection step for analyzing errors and revising navigation strategies.

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.

name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.

name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.

name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.

name: FingerTip 20K: A Benchmark for Proactive and Personalized Mobile LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: FingerTip 20K gathers 20K human Android demonstrations from users' long-term everyday app use, with user context, to evaluate proactive task suggestion and preference-aware task execution.

name: OdysseyBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Complex Office Application Workflows
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces OdysseyBench for evaluating long-horizon workflows across office applications, plus HomerAgents to generate tasks from environment exploration and dialogue synthesis.

name: PG-Agent: An Agent Powered by Page Graph
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces PG-Agent, which turns GUI operation episodes into page graphs and retrieves guidance from them to support task decomposition in new scenarios.

name: ReSum: Unlocking Long-Horizon Search Intelligence via Context Summarization
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ReSum, which compresses interaction histories during long web searches, and ReSum-GRPO, which trains agents to reason across the resulting segments.

name: PAL-UI: Planning with Active Look-back for Vision-Based GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.

name: GUI-KV: Efficient GUI Agents via KV Cache with Spatio-Temporal Awareness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

name: JEF-Hinter: Leveraging Offline Knowledge for Improving Web Agents Adaptation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces JEF-Hinter, which distills successful and failed trajectories into compact episodic hints and retrieves them for the current agent state. Web benchmark experiments examine guidance from decisive steps.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.

name: Genesis: Evolving Attack Strategies for LLM Web Agent Red-Teaming
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The experiments concern attacks across web tasks.
summary: Introduces Genesis, a red-teaming framework that generates adversarial injections for web agents and revises attack strategies using responses and interaction logs.

name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.

name: See, Think, Act: Online Shopper Behavior Simulation with VLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study concerns simulated shopper behavior and action prediction.
summary: Studies online shopper action prediction with VLM agents using webpage screenshots, HTML, and action history from OPeRA, trained with SFT and hierarchical RL rewards.

name: GUI-Rise: Structured Reasoning and History Summarization for GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Combines structured progress-and-decision reasoning with history summarization to improve cross-domain generalization in GUI navigation agents.

name: History-Aware Reasoning for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

name: WebCoach: Self-Evolving Web Agents with Cross-Session Memory Guidance
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebCoach, which condenses navigation logs into persistent episodic memory and retrieves experiences by similarity and recency. Runtime hooks selectively supply advice to browser agents, evaluated on WebVoyager without retraining the underlying models.

name: Real-Time Procedural Learning From Experience for AI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports only preliminary generalization to unseen tasks in similar environments.
summary: PRAXIS stores action outcomes and retrieves past state-action-result examples to guide agent decisions, with evaluation on the REAL web browsing benchmark.

name: HiconAgent: History Context-aware Policy Optimization for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: HiconAgent trains GUI policies to use history through variable-length context sampling and paired policy updates with compressed and complete histories. Its compression retains past actions while removing historical observations, and an alignment loss couples the two branches.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.

name: Me-Agent: A Personalized Mobile Agent with Two-Level User Habit Learning for Enhanced Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Me-Agent personalizes mobile agent behavior through a preference reward model and hierarchical memory for long-term and app-specific habits, and introduces User FingerTip.

name: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: MUZZLE evaluates web-agent exposure to indirect prompt injection by finding attack surfaces in agent trajectories and refining injected instructions from execution feedback.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions.

name: Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Efficient High-Resolution GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: GUIPruner compresses high-resolution screenshots and interaction history for GUI navigation through training-free resizing and layout-aware token pruning.

name: ST-Lite: Training-Free KV Cache Compression with Spatio-Trajectory Guidance for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3).
summary: Introduces ST-Lite, a training-free KV cache compression scheme for vision-language GUI agents that filters redundant frames and preserves small UI elements in interaction traces.

name: M$^2$: Dual-Memory Augmentation for Long-Horizon Web Agents via Trajectory Summarization and Insight Retrieval
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces M², a training-free memory framework for long-horizon web agents that summarizes interaction history and retrieves task guidance from an offline insight bank.

name: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Hierarchical Memory Tree (HMT), which organizes web-agent trajectories by intent, stage and action, then uses the hierarchy to plan and act on websites.

name: Ares: Adaptive Reasoning Effort Selection for Efficient LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). WebArena web-agent tasks are evaluated alongside tool-use and deep-research tasks.
summary: Introduces Ares, a router that selects a reasoning level for each step of a general LLM agent from its interaction history, with web agents among the evaluation settings.

name: Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces HyMEM, a graph-based memory for GUI agents that links symbolic task knowledge with trajectory embeddings and refreshes working memory during computer-use tasks.

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.

name: Read More, Think More: Revisiting Observation Reduction for Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies HTML and accessibility-tree observations for web agents, relating their usefulness to model capability and thinking budget, and proposes diff-based observation history to save tokens.

name: Same Outcomes, Different Journeys: A Trace-Level Framework for Comparing Human and GUI-Agent Behavior in Production Search Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The framework is instantiated in one audio-streaming search application with 39 participants and ten tasks.
summary: Presents a trace-level framework for comparing GUI agents with people on task outcomes, queries, and interface navigation in a production audio-search application.

name: Step-level Optimization for Efficient Computer-use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Proposes a step-level model cascade that runs a smaller computer-use policy until learned monitors flag stalled progress or semantic drift. Separate history-based stuck detection and milestone checks determine when to escalate for recovery or verification without retraining the larger model.

name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.

name: SimPersona: Learning Discrete Buyer Personas from Raw Clickstreams for Grounded E-Commerce Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported evaluation covers held-out live storefronts and buyer behavior.
summary: SimPersona learns buyer types from clickstreams and uses persona tokens to condition web agents trained on browsing traces for live storefront tasks.

name: Known By Their Actions: Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported identification results come from four web environments.
summary: A study shows that websites can infer the model behind a browser agent from passively recorded UI actions and timing traces across web tasks.

name: SE-GA: Memory-Augmented Self-Evolution for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: SE-GA retrieves hierarchical memories during inference and uses the collected experience in a separate policy-improvement pipeline. Its evaluation includes offline grounding/action tasks and online Android interaction, which measure different capabilities.

name: DiagEval: Trajectory-Conditioned Diagnosis for Reliable Software Evaluation with GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: DiagEval diagnoses failed GUI-agent evaluations of interactive software by reusing failed trajectories for targeted probes that distinguish execution errors from defects.

name: MementoGUI: Learning Agentic Multimodal Memory Control for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MementoGUI learns a controller for selecting, compressing and retrieving textual and region-level visual memories while leaving the GUI-agent backbone fixed. It also converts computer-use traces into controller training data and evaluates semantic actions, progress and memory consistency on long-horizon tasks.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.

name: Scaling, Benchmarking, and Reasoning of Vision-Language Agents for Mobile GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUIEvalKit benchmarks offline navigation tasks.
summary: HyperTrack provides mobile GUI navigation tasks across Chinese apps, while GUIEvalKit benchmarks VLM agents offline and supports analysis of training scale and history.

name: Masking Stale Observations Helps Search Agents -- Until It Doesn't: A Regime Map and Its Mechanism
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies when masking older retrieved pages helps long-horizon search agents manage context, using offline and live-web search benchmarks and analysis of reopened pages.

name: STaR-KV: Spatio-Temporal Adaptive Re-weighting for KV Cache Compression in GUI Vision-Language Models
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: STaR-KV compresses GUI-agent KV caches by calibrating visual-token importance across attention subspaces and interaction time. Its training-free scoring combines spatial specialization, temporal redundancy and an adaptive temperature, evaluated at matched cache budgets.

name: Online Skill Learning for Web Agents via State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: State-Grounded Dynamic Retrieval extracts reusable sub-procedures from completed web trajectories and represents them as paired text and code. Skills are retrieved against both the current webpage state and the task goal at intermediate execution steps.

name: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: HiViG combines a compact history of completed actions with a visually grounded critic that checks proposed coordinates before execution. Its evaluations separate history-related planning failures from errors caused by targeting the wrong screen element.

name: A Benchmark and Framework for Evaluating Next Action Predictions in Spreadsheets
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a benchmark and online evaluation method for predicting the next spreadsheet action from a user's action history, using curated action sequences.

name: Naive Visual Memory is Not Enough: A Failure-Mode Study of GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study finds that full-image visual memory can reduce some state errors while worsening action-level failures. Its AGMem alternative stores local crops associated with successful actions or recovery and evaluates their use in desktop GUI tasks.

name: MemGUI-Agent: An End-to-End Long-Horizon Mobile GUI Agent with Proactive Context Management
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: MemGUI-Agent makes context management an action chosen by the same policy that controls the mobile UI. Structured history, UI-state and recent-step fields are trained from annotated trajectories to retain cross-app facts while limiting context growth.

name: BaRA: Budget-constrained and Reliable Web Data Collection Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its focus is site-level data collection within an interaction budget.
summary: Introduces BaRA, a web data-collection agent that discovers live site links, checks extracted text, images, and videos, and uses history to recover from failures.

name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: KnowAct-GUIClaw combines a host planner with pluggable GUI subagents, attributable experience memory and an evolving skill library. It uses user profiles and feedback for task decomposition and evaluates transfer across Android, iOS, HarmonyOS and Windows.

name: PersonaTrail: Benchmarking Personalized Web Agents through Browsing Trails
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces PersonaTrail, a benchmark for personalized web agents using browsing histories, and PACMem, a structured memory method for guiding navigation.

name: Qwen-CUA: Native Computer Use for (almost) Everything
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Qwen-CUA operates through screenshots and keyboard/mouse events while compressing older visual history into reusable context blocks. Its report combines verifiable task generation, trajectory-based training and separate browser and Bash-augmented studies.

name: Screenshots or Tools? Eliciting Tool Use and Managing Multimodal Context in Hybrid GUI-MCP Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: This study separates tool-adoption behavior from task competence in hybrid GUI–MCP agents. It tests tool-use incentives and screenshot-history compression, showing that changed action preferences can coexist with unchanged held-out accuracy.

name: FocusMem: Factorizing Content, Readout, and Trust in Latent GUI Memory
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its components are trained while the GUI policy remains frozen.
summary: Introduces FocusMem, a latent memory interface for GUI agents that separates stored content, state-conditioned readout, and a gate for irrelevant retrieved experience.

name: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Gated Hindsight Distillation gives a teacher access to the next screenshot during training while the student sees only the available trajectory prefix. Distillation is applied when hindsight repairs a student failure, and the resulting policies are evaluated on Android tasks.

name: MemPrism: Task-Conditioned Relational Memory Views for Long-Horizon Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The reported experiments also include embodied-agent benchmarks.
summary: Introduces MemPrism, which records prior interactions and builds task-conditioned relational memory views for decisions in long-horizon web-agent tasks.

name: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Task Model Induction disentangles concurrent activities in screenshot and mouse/keyboard traces, then constructs hierarchical goals and procedural control flow for each task. Evaluation tests reconstruction of observed execution and reuse of derived skills on held-out tasks.

name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.

name: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: GraphDroid combines clustered memory of visited GUI states with asynchronous test-intent generation. A hybrid executor reserves LLM calls for complex intents and uses heuristics for simpler ones, evaluated through Android app coverage, bug discovery and crash detection.

name: TRACE: Trajectory-robust Admission with Evidence Ordering for Efficient GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: TRACE orders screenshot evidence for monotonic visual-token reduction using layout priors, instruction relevance and feature novelty. Spatial token reserves and incremental KV contraction aim to preserve useful evidence for future GUI targets without repeatedly encoding retired frames.

name: AnchorGUI: Asymmetric Memory for Dual-Scale Learning in GUI Navigation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: AnchorGUI compares expected and observed UI transitions and selectively retains screenshots when they disagree. This asymmetric memory supports immediate correction and focuses cross-attempt experience distillation on likely failure steps.

name: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: GUI-SD-v2 extends on-policy self-distillation from grounding to multi-turn GUI interaction. It first strengthens responses to privileged guidance, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory support for later actions.

name: SimTrace: Grounded Multimodal User Trajectories Generation for Online User Modeling
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract evaluates SimTrace in an e-commerce setting.
summary: Introduces SimTrace, a framework that generates synthetic multimodal web clickstreams by pairing a computer-use client agent's actions with web observations and user context.

name: ReSAIL: Mitigating Collapse in Iterative Agent Self-Distillation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). GUI action prediction on AITZ is a secondary test; the main experiments use ALFWorld and TextCraft.
summary: Introduces ReSAIL, an augmentation for iterative agent self-distillation that selects informative interaction steps; it also tests GUI-agent action prediction.

notes: Adjacent diagnostic research across simulators, policies, tools, coding and an offline Mind2Web subset. Models choose among supplied admissible actions in the reported evaluation. The paired probes measure selected visible facts. Pooled results cover multiple settings, and the paper reports coverage limits and label-sensitivity analyses. No benchmark release, code, data or weights were independently inspected.
summary: Pairs factual probes with next-action choices on frozen agent traces, including Mind2Web, to diagnose reading-decision gaps without closed-loop execution.

name: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
notes: A broad literature synthesis spanning images, video, audio, GUI and embodied settings. Its GUI section compares interface-state retention, action outcomes, cross-session reuse and visual evidence; the paper is a literature synthesis. Taxonomy corpus counts and benchmark classifications are authors’ annotations. Updating stored content is one memory operation; the survey’s self-evolving-policy tier and memory’s contribution to endpoint task success require separate evidence. Lifecycle, resource-budget and provenance recommendations are proposed evaluation directions. Platform facets remain unspecified.
summary: Surveys multimodal memory using representation and management axes, distinguishing fixed-policy updates from policy evolution and comparing GUI memory evaluation with other modalities.

name: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
notes: Privileged screenshot history is used during training, while deployment retains self-generated textual state. GUI results use action/step metrics and model-specific history settings; online Sokoban transfer is separate. GRPO rewards action correctness, valid output format and compression length. Diagnostic memory replay is distinct from the validation gap used to schedule training.
summary: ECHOES learns recursive textual task memory through privileged screenshot-history distillation and GRPO, then predicts GUI actions from the current screenshot and memory.

name: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected v1 method/evaluation sections. OmniGUI uses episode-disjoint reference-action evaluation with Type Match, Exact Match and Goal Progress; live task-success gains remain unestablished. The Android role is explicit in Appendix D.1.
summary: FocusGUI learns step-specific weights over screenshot, audio, video and interaction-context channels, injecting a compact residual into a frozen decoder without pruning its inputs.

name: ScopeMem: Latent Memory That Learns Where to Revise Frozen GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 controlled-study, method and limitations sections. Results are offline, step-level action matching; online task success is explicitly left untested. The frozen actor is queried twice per step.
summary: ScopeMem conditions latent-memory prefixes on a frozen GUI agent's initial action and trains them to correct errors while preserving correct decisions. Its evaluation separates action repairs from harmful revisions.

name: Subgoal-aware Memory Graph for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Evaluation is reported on SPA-Bench.
summary: Proposes a subgoal-aware memory graph that turns past mobile GUI agent trajectories into reusable evidence for decisions across tasks.

name: Reuse, Rewrite, or Reject: Evidence-Constrained Trace Reuse for Repeated Mobile GUI Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The abstract reports results on AndroidWorld and real Android and HarmonyOS devices.
summary: Proposes graph-text templates that let mobile GUI agents reuse, adapt, or discard steps from earlier executions based on the current instruction and UI state.

name: iPrefBench: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personalized Mobile Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its tasks use an interactive simulated user and a constructed activity history.
summary: Introduces iPrefBench, an iOS benchmark for mobile agents that tests when they infer missing user preferences from activity history and when they ask the user.

name: GUIFlow: Temporal Redundancy-Aware Incremental Inference for GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported speedups cover offline multi-image benchmarks and closed-loop OSWorld runs.
summary: Introduces GUIFlow, an incremental inference framework that reuses visual, language, and action computation across successive GUI-agent steps.

name: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MemU-Bench for mobile GUI tasks that depend on past user interactions, alongside AppMem, a training-free memory framework for retrieving app-specific context.

name: MAPLE: A Multimodal Mobile Agent with Playbook-Learned Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces MAPLE, a training-free multi-agent framework that shares step-level experience while navigating mobile GUIs and updates prompts during execution.

name: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Web Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported experiments use WebArena, WebVoyager, and WebShop.
summary: Introduces SCOPE, a training method for long web-agent tasks that discovers local skills from rollouts, composes them into chains, and expands them using failure experience.

name: Can LLM Agents Learn to Test? Maintaining Scoped Experience as Testing Evidence for Mobile GUI Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).

name: UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the EMNLP 2025 proceedings page and the full proceedings PDF. The PDF (10.9 MB) exceeds the receipt size limit, so the retained receipt is the landing page with its complete abstract. Per the PDF, UI-Hawk replaces TextHawk's language model with Qwen2-7B and encodes each history screenshot at a quarter of its size in 144 visual tokens; FunUI holds 2,150 Chinese and 9,347 English Android screens, and navigation is evaluated on GUI-Odyssey+ (GUIOdyssey clicks re-annotated with element boxes) and the authors' Chinese GUI-Zouwu episodes. An earlier version titled 'UI-Hawk: Unleashing the Screen Stream Understanding for GUI Agents' was posted on Preprints.org on 30 August 2024 (DOI 10.20944/preprints202408.2137.v1) by the same six authors. The paper points to github.com/IMNearth/UIHawk for code and data.
summary: Mobile GUI agent whose history-aware visual encoder reads earlier screenshots with the current one, trained by a curriculum from grounding, referring, screen QA and summarization to navigation; adds the FunUI benchmark.
